source.title: Architecture, Not Scale: Circuit Localization in Large Language Models

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates IOI circuit concentration in other model families using head ablations, but does not reproduce the original GPT-2 small activation-patching analysis or its faithfulness, completeness and minimality tests.
record.gate_note: The study measures IOI behavior and head-ablation effects in six Pythia and Qwen2.5 models. It does not test GPT-2 small or identify the original circuit's seven head classes and roles. Results on induction and factual recall are not recorded as separate IOI findings; the reported comparison of top IOI and induction heads is included because it bears on component reuse. Prior-work results are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study runs IOI head ablations on Pythia and Qwen2.5, but it only measures circuit concentration: top-head logit-difference drop and greedy heads-to-80%. It never assigns heads to roles such as name-mover, S-inhibition or duplicate-token, never tests GPT-2 small, and never asks whether the original circuit's classes recur. Concentration is a related but different construct from V3's 'same head classes and roles'. Concentration alone cannot show whether the same circuit is present. No other version is probed. It is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a test.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that attention architecture (GQA vs MHA) predicts circuit concentration and stability more reliably than parameter count, across IOI, induction and factual recall. They also report a phase transition in Qwen2.5 factual recall between 0.5B and 1.5B. They acknowledge that training data, tokenizer and recipe confound the architecture comparison. Input-difficulty instability is shown for Pythia factual recall, not for IOI.
record.recipe_differences: Uses head-ablation scores and greedy heads-to-80% curves on Pythia and Qwen2.5, rather than the original GPT-2 small activation-patching circuit analysis and its faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported IOI concentration differs across the tested MHA and GQA model families; the study does not vary the IOI prompt distribution or ablation method.

fits_no_version.finding: IOI head-ablation damage is concentrated in one head or layer band in Qwen2.5 (GQA): heads-to-80% is 1 for all three sizes, and the top head is at L23 for 0.5B and L0 for 1.5B and 7B. In Pythia (MHA), heads-to-80% is 2 to 5 with smaller top-head drops.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI circuit concentration under head ablation depends on attention architecture (GQA vs MHA) more than on parameter count.

record.problems: The study does not include GPT-2 small or test the original circuit's named head classes and roles. It reports no uncertainty estimates for the IOI results. Pythia and Qwen2.5 differ in training data, tokenizer and training recipe as well as attention architecture, a confound the authors acknowledge.
record.rows_left_out: No additional IOI result rows omitted. Non-IOI induction and factual-recall ablation results are outside the IOI claim; only the reported cross-task top-head comparison is included.

untested.parts: All of it: GPT-2 small is not studied, and neither are its 26 heads, 7 classes, or the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
All of it: no name-mover ablation and no backup-head analysis.
Whether IOI head classes and roles recur in Pythia or Qwen2.5; checkpoints; component reuse across tasks.
All of it: no comparison of circuit-finding methods, ablation types or metrics.
All of it for IOI: ablation type, metric and prompt distribution are not varied.
All of it: no variation of name order, template or number of names.

record.verdict_notes: The ablation type ('value zeroing' is mentioned) is not fully specified. In Qwen2.5, ablating a layer-0 KV head removes all query heads that share it, so the damage may reflect a generic early-layer bottleneck rather than an IOI-specific component. Heads are scored on only 20 sentences, and no uncertainty is reported. The reader's V3 labels are dropped: concentration counts do not test head-class identity, and the top-head mismatch with induction does not test reuse.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test GPT-2 small, its 26-head/seven-class circuit, or the original faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
It does not ablate the original main name-mover heads or test backup name-mover self-repair.

It tests IOI circuit concentration in other model families and compares top IOI and induction heads, but does not identify whether the original head classes and semantic roles are present in those models, assess other checkpoints, or establish reuse beyond the reported top-head comparison.
It does not compare circuit-finding methods, ablation types or evaluation metrics.
It does not vary IOI ablation method, metric or prompt distribution to test evaluation sensitivity.
It does not compare IOI name orders, templates or numbers of names.

rows.subject: Pythia and Qwen2.5 models (all six; aggregate as reported)
rows.operation_detail: Compared the top-scoring IOI head with the top-scoring induction-task head.

conditions.value: IOI and random repeated-token induction task
all six Pythia and Qwen2.5 models

rows.measure: Whether the top-scoring head is the same across the two tasks
rows.value: The top-scoring IOI and induction heads are different in all six models.
rows.note: This comparison concerns top-scoring individual heads and does not establish whether other circuit components are shared.
rows.check: The top IOI head differing from the top induction head does not test component reuse. In the original circuit, induction heads are an upstream class while the top IOI head would be a name mover, so this result is consistent with reuse. The 'absent' state and the 'challenges' label are unwarranted.
